small_guidance:
- The conv kernel writes a per-tile partial sum (N, OC, NUM_HW) only to read it back in `reduce_partials_kernel`; fuse the HW reduction into `conv_transpose2d_pool_kernel` by using `tl.atomic_add` into a (N, OC) pooled buffer (or grid-z loop inside the kernel) so the partial materialization and second pass disappear.
- Add `triton.autotune` over BLOCK_OC ∈ {64,128}, BLOCK_HW ∈ {64,128,256}, BLOCK_IC ∈ {16,32,64}, num_warps ∈ {4,8}, num_stages ∈ {2,3} keyed on (OC, OHW, IC); current 64/128/32 is unlikely optimal for OHW≈263k.
- The dominant cost is the conv loop body: hoist `pid_n*IC*IH*IW` and the kh/kw constants out of the `ic_start` loop, and switch the GEMM to accumulate with `tl.dot(..., acc, out_dtype=tl.float32)` form to enable mma pipelining.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as a true scatter-add ConvTranspose2d fused with the spatial mean: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile) loads x once, multiplies by the (IC, OC, KH, KW) weight, and `tl.atomic_add`s the OC-vector contribution directly into a (N, OC) accumulator (since every output position is summed anyway, you can skip computing OH×OW entirely and just accumulate Σ over scattered positions per (n, oc)). This still does the full IC·OC·KH·KW·IH·IW MACs the reference requires but eliminates the OH×OW write/read traffic that dominates 39 ms.
- Boundary handling: only KH·KW − (KH−1+KW−1)·something positions are border; treat the interior (where all kh,kw contribute) as a single GEMM `(N·IH·IW, IC) @ (IC, OC)` scaled by KH·KW, then add small correction kernels for the borders. This converts most of the work into a dense IC×OC GEMM that cuBLAS-class Triton GEMMs handle well.
- Use channels-last (NHWC) layout for x and (IC, OC) packed weight so the GEMM-K (=IC) dimension is contiguous and loads coalesce; fuse the mean division, bias add, logsumexp over OC, and ×10 into a tiny finalize kernel that runs over N only.
